incident-bot: ALERT: High tail latency detected for hosted text-generation (region: us-west-2). p95 > 800ms, p99 > 2.5s. Possible KV cache pressure spike. Paging oncall. /incidents/1839998765

eric_oncall: I'm on it, taking the page. starting with recent deploys and runtime metrics. anyone seeing deploys in last 30m?

lina_sre: not from infra side. I can pull evictions and cache fill stats. grabbing graphs now.

oliver_runtime: seeing an increase in cache_evictions/sec and a large number of small-value entries. Prefill rate looks normal but decode time per token spiked for some hosts. streaming stalls correlate with high eviction bursts.

maya_prod: customer signal: a handful of streaming sessions reported stalls and reconnects, ~0.4% of active sessions (higher for users on long-context). No error 5xx, just timeouts on client side.

eric_oncall: ok that matches SLO breaches for streaming tail. can you paste the eviction query, @lina_sre ?

lina_sre: metrics query (prom):
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)
sum(rate(kv_cache_prefills_total[1m])) by (shard)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(decode_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,host))
```

lina_sre: quick snapshot: evictions spiked to ~12k/min on shard-7, prefill steady, decode p99 jumped from 450ms -> 2.2s on same shard.

raj_infra: shard-7 has higher fragmentation; free segments fragmented after recent GC job. Possible allocation pressure from many small context keys.

oliver_runtime: hypothesis: prefill << decode imbalance. During heavy decode, the runtime aggressively allocates KV slots for in-flight tokens; background prefill isn't keeping hot prefixes warm, so we see thrashing: entries evicted while needed for decode, causing extra recompute and stalls.

eric_oncall: what's the immediate mitigation we can do? Can we bump cache capacity or change eviction policy?

raj_infra: we can temporarily increase cache capacity on shard-7 by attaching the spare capacity pool. doing that now (will take ~60s to rebalance).

oliver_runtime: also suggest switching eviction policy to LRU-strict on that shard to favor longer-lived prefixes. Risk: may increase memory pressure elsewhere but OK for short window.

maya_prod: customers want ETA and mitigation update. please post message for support.

eric_oncall: will update. quick mitigation plan: 1) attach spare capacity to shard-7 (raj) 2) switch eviction -> LRU-strict on shard-7 (oliver) 3) ramp fallback routing to smaller model variant for streaming sessions from affected region (maya), 4) increase decode timeouts and add short prefill boost for long-context sessions.

raj_infra: spare capacity attached. mem usage stabilizing. evictions dropped 70% in last 90s.

oliver_runtime: eviction policy flipped on shard-7. monitoring decode p99...

lina_sre: decode p99 trending down: 2.2s -> 620ms in 3m. streaming stall rate dropping.

eric_oncall: good. starting customer impact note for support: affected ~0.4% sessions, major impact window ~10:12-10:25 UTC, mitigations applied.

maya_prod: posted to support thread and notified enterprise contacts. added workaround: recommend clients set streaming reconnect to exponential backoff for next 24h.

oliver_runtime: follow-up: we need to investigate fragmentation root cause. candidate causes: GC scheduling change, increased small-prefix workload from new demo, or a bug in prefill prioritization.

raj_infra: I'll dig into GC job logs and allocation histograms for shard-7.

lina_sre: capturing diagnostics: heap snapshots, KV occupancy histograms, per-prefix ttl distribution. linking artifacts to incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1839998765/artifacts

eric_oncall: handoff: I need to go offline in 20m. @lina_sre please take lead, @oliver_runtime you're primary for runtime changes. leave a compact handoff note: what to watch (p95/p99, evictions/sec, decode_latency p99), and rollback plan for eviction policy.

lina_sre: got it. brief handoff: watch metrics above, if evictions rise >8k/min revert eviction policy and scale capacity. if decode p99 > 2s re-enable routing fallback to smaller model for affected sessions. I'll open a short-lived runbook in the ticket.

eric_oncall: thanks. posting final summary to incidents channel then leaving.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied by raj_infra and oliver_runtime. Customer impact reduced. Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 at 10:28 UTC. Postmortem requested within 72h.

oliver_runtime: notes for postmortem: quantify prefill vs decode rates over window, trace a few affected sessions end-to-end, check for regression from last runtime change 2 days ago (prefill prioritizer tweak).

lina_sre: will collect timelines and own postmortem. assigning to runtime+infra.

maya_prod: closing customer updates. will reopen if any enterprise reports regressions.

eric_oncall: handoff complete, leaving the channel. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
